title: सरकारलाई कांग्रेसको प्रश्न- नागरिकको जीवनसँग जोडिएको विषयमा उदासीनता कहिलेसम्म ?
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । प्रमुख प्रतिपक्षी दल नेपाली कांग्रेस संसदीय दलका नेता भीष्मराज आङदेम्बेले मकवानपुर दुर्घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी दोषीको पहिचान गर्न र सत्यतथ्य सार्वजनिक गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन्। मकवानपुरको चिसापानीगढीमा यात्रुवाहक ईभी हाइस दुर्घटनामा हुँदा १४ जनाको मृत्यु र ६ जना घाइते भएका थिए। उनले दुर्घटनाको कारण पत्ता लगाउन सवारीसाधनमा क्षमताभन्दा बढी यात्रु राखिएको थियो वा थिएन, सवारीको प्राविधिक अवस्था कस्तो थियो र यात्रुको विवरण प्रहरी चेकपोस्टमा किन अद्यावधिक गरिएन भन्ने विषयमा प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। आङदेम्बेले आज जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘आखिर यो दुर्घटनामा कसको के कमजोरी रह्यो ? क्षमताभन्दा बढी यात्रु राखिएको थियो कि थिएन ? सवारीको प्राविधिक अवस्था कस्तो थियो ? यात्रुको विवरण प्रहरी चेकपोस्टमा किन अद्यावधिक गरिएन ? चेकपोस्टमा खटिएका प्रहरी र सम्बन्धित निकायले आफ्नो जिम्मेवारी किन पूरा गरेनन् ? यी सबै प्रश्नको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गरी सत्यतथ्य सार्वजनिक गर्नुपर्छ ।’ उनले यसअघि रोल्पाको जलजलामा भएको दुर्घटनामा २० जनाले ज्यान गुमाउँदा पनि सरकारले छानबिन समिति बनाएको तर अझै प्रतिवेदन सार्वजनिक नगरिएको भन्दै प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। ‘न दुर्घटनाको कारण सार्वजनिक भयो, न भविष्यमा यस्ता दुर्घटना रोक्न सरकारले के कदम चाल्यो भन्ने जानकारी दिइयो’ विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘हरेक दुर्घटनापछि छानबिन समिति बनाउने, केही दिन चर्चा गर्ने र त्यसपछि घटनालाई बिर्सने सरकारी प्रवृत्तिको अन्त्य हुनुपर्छ ।’ नागरिकको ज्यान जोगाउनु सरकारको पहिलो दायित्व भएको उनको भनाइ छ। विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘सडक सुरक्षा, सवारीको प्राविधिक परीक्षण, यात्रुको विवरण अभिलेख र प्रहरीको निगरानी प्रभावकारी बनाउन सरकार किन गम्भीर हुँदैन ? नागरिकको जीवनसँग जोडिएको विषयमा सरकारको यस्तो उदासीनता कहिलेसम्म ? अब सडक सुरक्षामा ठोस सुधार आवश्यक छ । राज्यले नागरिकको जीवनको मूल्य बुझ्नुपर्छ ।’ दुर्घटनामा घाइते भएकाको उपचारमा कुनै कमी हुन नदिन र सम्पूर्ण उपचारको व्यवस्था मिलाउन सरकारसँग आग्रह गरेका छन्। Kathmandu. Bhishma Raj Angdembe, leader of the parliamentary party of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, has demanded that the government conduct an impartial investigation into the Makawanpur accident and identify the culprits and make the truth public. Fourteen people were killed and six injured when a passenger EV bus crashed in Chisapanigarhi, Makawanpur. He has raised questions about whether the vehicle was overloaded, what the technical condition of the vehicle was, and why the passenger details were not updated at the police checkpoint to determine the cause of the accident. In a statement issued today, Angdembe said, "Whose fault was it in this accident? Were there more passengers than capacity? What was the technical condition of the vehicle? Why were the passenger details not updated at the police check post? Why did the police and related agencies deployed at the check post not fulfill their responsibilities? All these questions should be investigated impartially and the truth should be made public." He has previously raised questions, saying that the government has formed an investigation committee after 20 people lost their lives in an accident in Jaljala, Rolpa, but the report has not been made public yet. "Neither the cause of the accident was made public, nor was information provided on what steps the government has taken to prevent such accidents in the future," the statement said. "The government's tendency to form an investigation committee after every accident, discuss it for a few days, and then forget about the incident must end." He says that the government's first responsibility is to protect the lives of citizens. The statement said, "Why is the government not serious about making road safety, technical inspection of vehicles, recording passenger details, and police surveillance effective? How long will the government remain indifferent to issues related to the lives of citizens? Concrete improvements in road safety are now necessary. The state must understand the value of citizens' lives." They have urged the government to ensure that there is no shortage in the treatment of those injured in the accident and to make arrangements for full treatment.

विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘सडक सुरक्षा, सवारीको प्राविधिक परीक्षण, यात्रुको विवरण अभिलेख र प्रहरीको निगरानी प्रभावकारी बनाउन सरकार किन गम्भीर हुँदैन ? नागरिकको जीवनसँग जोडिएको विषयमा सरकारको यस्तो उदासीनता कहिलेसम्म ? अब सडक सुरक्षामा ठोस सुधार आवश्यक छ । राज्यले नागरिकको जीवनको मूल्य बुझ्नुपर्छ ।’

दुर्घटनामा घाइते भएकाको उपचारमा कुनै कमी हुन नदिन र सम्पूर्ण उपचारको व्यवस्था मिलाउन सरकारसँग आग्रह गरेका छन्।

Kathmandu. Bhishma Raj Angdembe, leader of the parliamentary party of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, has demanded that the government conduct an impartial investigation into the Makawanpur accident and identify the culprits and make the truth public. Fourteen people were killed and six injured when a passenger EV bus crashed in Chisapanigarhi, Makawanpur. He has raised questions about whether the vehicle was overloaded, what the technical condition of the vehicle was, and why the passenger details were not updated at the police checkpoint to determine the cause of the accident. In a statement issued today, Angdembe said, "Whose fault was it in this accident? Were there more passengers than capacity? What was the technical condition of the vehicle? Why were the passenger details not updated at the police check post? Why did the police and related agencies deployed at the check post not fulfill their responsibilities? All these questions should be investigated impartially and the truth should be made public." He has previously raised questions, saying that the government has formed an investigation committee after 20 people lost their lives in an accident in Jaljala, Rolpa, but the report has not been made public yet. "Neither the cause of the accident was made public, nor was information provided on what steps the government has taken to prevent such accidents in the future," the statement said. "The government's tendency to form an investigation committee after every accident, discuss it for a few days, and then forget about the incident must end." He says that the government's first responsibility is to protect the lives of citizens. The statement said, "Why is the government not serious about making road safety, technical inspection of vehicles, recording passenger details, and police surveillance effective? How long will the government remain indifferent to issues related to the lives of citizens? Concrete improvements in road safety are now necessary. The state must understand the value of citizens' lives." They have urged the government to ensure that there is no shortage in the treatment of those injured in the accident and to make arrangements for full treatment.
